title: bit-halving recursion is independent of the fuel, given two sufficient fuels
statement: For any carrier alpha, base value z, step function f, and naturals fuel1, n, fuel2: if n <= fuel1 and n <= fuel2, then binaryRecAux alpha z f fuel1 n = binaryRecAux alpha z f fuel2 n.

formal.statement: theorem Nat.binaryRecAux_agree_of_fuel : ((x0 : Sort (1)) -> ((x1 : x0) -> ((x2 : ((x2 : Bool) -> ((x3 : AxNat) -> ((x4 : x0) -> x0)))) -> ((x3 : AxNat) -> ((x4 : AxNat) -> ((x5 : AxNat) -> ((x6 : AxNat.le x4 x3) -> ((x7 : AxNat.le x4 x5) -> Eq.{1} x0 (AxNat.binaryRecAux x0 x1 x2 x3 x4) (AxNat.binaryRecAux x0 x1 x2 x5 x4)))))))))

notes:
formal.statement is `Kernel::render_lean` of the admitted type, taken verbatim from `nat_theorem_inventory`, not transcribed by hand. `AxNat` is the kernel's CONSTRUCTED inductive `Nat` (the `Ax` is *axeyum*, not *axiomatized*).

`Nat.binaryRecAux` (`nat_prelude/binary_rec.rs`) is bit-halving recursion carried on an explicit fuel counter: `binaryRecAux alpha z f 0 n = z`, `binaryRecAux alpha z f (succ k) 0 = z`, and `binaryRecAux alpha z f (succ k) (succ m) = f (beq ((succ m) % 2) 1) ((succ m) / 2) (binaryRecAux alpha z f k ((succ m) / 2))` -- all three definitional. `Nat.binaryRec alpha z f n := binaryRecAux alpha z f n n` supplies the canonical fuel.

The DOUBLE-fuel form is forced, not stylistic: the canonical instance puts `n` itself in the fuel slot, so a 'fuel versus the canonical instance' statement refers to itself and its induction cannot unfold. Two independently-chosen sufficient fuels have no such self-reference. Proved by `agree_by_fuel_induction` (`nat_prelude/ops.rs`) on `fuel1` with `n` and `fuel2` both generalized in the motive; at `fuel1 = 0` the hypothesis `Le n 0` forces `n = 0` (`le_antisymm`/`zero_le`) and both sides collapse via `binaryRecAux_zero`; at `fuel1 = succ k` a `cases_zero_succ` on `n` handles `n = 0` the same way and, at `n = succ m`, derives `fuel2 = succ (pred fuel2)` from positivity (`succ_pred_of_pos`), bounds both halves by `Nat.half_le_of_succ_le_succ`, applies the induction hypothesis at `(div (succ m) 2, pred fuel2)`, and closes with one congruence in the step function's third argument.

The `n = 0` guard in the definition is what makes this TRUE. Without it, fuel `succ k` at `n = 0` would apply `f` at `bit false 0 = 0` and the value would depend on how much fuel remained.

The hypotheses are not decoration: `binaryRecAux 0 n = z` for any `n`, while `binaryRec n` need not be, so the unconditional statement is false.

NOT a candidate to close `F:ml430-nat-fastfib-eq-cde11774` or any `binaryRec` mirror. Mathlib's `Nat.binaryRec` (`Mathlib/Data/Nat/BinaryRec.lean:88` at the pinned commit `c5ea00351c28e24afc9f0f84379aa41082b1188f`) is WELL-FOUNDED recursion on a `log2`-based measure with a DEPENDENT motive in an arbitrary `Sort u`; this is structural recursion on a fuel counter, non-dependent, with an extra fuel argument. Same values, different `def` -- the `Nat.multichoose`/`Nat.minFac` case of the mirror-flip criterion, not the `Nat.descFactorial_of_lt` case. A fuel encoding CANNOT be dependent: the fuel-exhaustion row must return a value for an arbitrary `n` and only `motive 0` is in hand.
